NIH Postdoctoral Fellowship in Medical Extended Reality and Immersive Simulation
Immersive Simulation Program / Social and Behavioral Research Branch / National Human Genome Research Institute / National Institutes of Health

How can we use the unique capabilities of immersive technologies to improve health research and healthcare? Join the Immersive Simulation Program to build, evaluate, and study the next generation of immersive research tools and health interventions.

Led by Dr. Susan Persky<

> is part of the NIH Intramural Research Program at NHGRI and collaborates across NIH to develop, evaluate, and study emerging technology-based research tools and health interventions. We seek a fellow with substantive research expertise in immersive or related technologies, including studies with human research participants.

Anticipated start: Summer 2027; earlier starts are also welcome.

Research Opportunities
The fellow will help develop, implement, and evaluate methods and research tools, analyze multimodal data, and communicate findings through manuscripts and presentations.
Potential areas include:
Methods and pipelines for generating and evaluating purpose-built virtual environments, experimental stimuli, and virtual agents
Analysis and integration of multimodal data (e.g., behavioral, physiological, eye tracking, wearable-based) to inform and assess research and clinical implementation of immersive technology
Theoretical and empirical work to establish best practices and models for the development and implementation of immersive technology in healthcare
Experimental research to expand understanding of media technology influences, human-computer interaction, and the psychology of immersive experience
You will have flexibility to develop research aligned with your interests while contributing to ongoing projects.

Required qualifications
A doctoral degree in computer science, human-computer interaction, biomedical engineering, cognitive science, psychology, communication, or a related field, received within 5 years of the fellowship start date
Demonstrated experience applying computational and/or AI/ML methods in research, including model development, adaptation, and evaluation
Strong data science and quantitative analysis skills, including experience preparing, analyzing, and interpreting complex datasets and proficiency in scientific programming (e.g., Python or R)
Experience conducting human subjects research
Excellent written and oral communication skills

Preferred experience:
Extended reality (XR) development experience using game engines such as Unity or Unreal, 3D content creation, and/or development of embodied conversational agents
Experience with physiological, sensor, wearable, or other multimodal behavioral data, including time-series analysis or integration of data streams
Expertise in research methods and experimental design
Familiarity with XR-relevant theory (e.g., presence, embodiment)

What we offer:
A full-time, on-site fellowship at the NIH campus in Bethesda, Maryland, with an initial one-year appointment that is renewable
Individualized mentorship from Dr. Susan Persky and professional development support aligned with your research interests and career goals
Opportunities to participate in basic and translational medical XR research, including clinical trial work conducted at the NIH Clinical Center
Access to scientific communities, seminars, training programs, research infrastructure, and interdisciplinary expertise across NHGRI and NIH
Stipend and benefits<

> consistent with NIH postdoctoral appointment policies

How to apply:
Email Dr. Susan Persky at

> and include:
Your CV
A statement of research interests describing your relevant experience, the research you hope to pursue in the fellowship, and how the position fits your career goals
Names and contact information for three professional references

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Applications received by December 1, 2026 will receive priority review. Please reference "immersive simulation position" in the email subject line or body when submitting application materials.

U.S. citizens, permanent residents, and eligible international applicants may apply, subject to current NIH appointment requirements and restrictions. NIH welcomes foreign nationals with the exception of individuals from countries on this list<
